This script prepares the data of the survey experiment before the 2025 federal election.
It writes three files to `data/processed/`, which `22_federal_descriptives.Rmd` reads:

- `results_official_federal.rdata`: the official second-vote result, the benchmark of all accuracy measures,
- `data_federal.rdata`: one row per respondent (first participation only) with all variables of the analyses,
- `data_federal_long.rdata`: one row per respondent and party with the expected vote share and the forecast error.

# Official Election Result

Second-vote shares of the 2025 federal election.
The numbers of second votes of the parties asked about in the survey and the number of valid second votes
are copied from the final result of the Federal Returning Officer
(<https://www.bundeswahlleiterin.de/bundestagswahlen/2025/ergebnisse/bund-99.html>)
to `data/input/results/btw25_second_votes_federal.csv`.
Shares are in % of the valid second votes.

```{r results_official_federal}
votes_federal <- read_csv("data/input/results/btw25_second_votes_federal.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

valid_second_votes_federal <- votes_federal %>%
  filter(party == "Valid second votes") %>%
  pull(votes)

results_official_federal <- votes_federal %>%
  filter(party != "Valid second votes") %>%
  mutate(party = if_else(party %in% c("CDU", "CSU"), "CDU/CSU", party)) %>% # CDU and CSU combined
  group_by(party) %>%
  summarize(votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    party = factor(party, levels = c("CDU/CSU", "AfD", "SPD", "Greens", "Left", "BSW", "FDP")),
    result_official = votes / valid_second_votes_federal * 100 # share of valid second votes in %
  ) %>%
  arrange(party) %>%
  mutate(party = as.character(party)) %>%
  select(-votes) %>%
  add_row(party = "Others", result_official = 100 - sum(.$result_official))
rm(votes_federal)

results_official_federal

save(results_official_federal, file = "data/processed/results_official_federal.rdata")
```


# Survey Data

## Sample

The analyses use each respondent's first participation in one of the two waves of the online access panel (`bilendi_w1`, `bilendi_w2`).
Respondents could take part more than once. Later participations are dropped, so no respondent saw the experiment twice.
The survey file contains only these interviews (one row per respondent):
the sample is selected in `01_create_replication_data.R` from the raw survey data, which are not public.

Party identification was asked only in the re-interviews of wave 2.
`01_create_replication_data.R` takes it from a respondent's second participation and joins it to the first participation
(`pid_date`: date of the re-interview, missing for respondents without a re-interview).
The output shows the number and field period of these re-interviews, then the size of the sample by wave.

```{r load}
load("data/input/survey/survey_federal.rdata")

# Field period of the re-interviews
survey_federal %>%
  filter(!is.na(pid_date)) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), first_day = min(pid_date), last_day = max(pid_date))

data_federal <- survey_federal %>%
  mutate(
    pid = case_when(
      is.na(pid) ~ NA_character_, # no re-interview or no answer
      pid == "AfD" ~ "AfD",
      pid == "BSW" ~ "BSW",
      pid == "CDU/CSU" ~ "CDU/CSU",
      pid == "FDP" ~ "FDP",
      pid == "GRÜNE" ~ "Greens",
      pid == "DIE LINKE" ~ "Left",
      pid == "SPD" ~ "SPD",
      pid == "Keiner Partei" ~ "none",
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-pid_date)

data_federal %>% count(source)
rm(survey_federal)
```

## Variables

Recodes of the variables used in the models:

- `treatment`: experimental group (Control, Treatment (5), Treatment (500)),
- `lead_time`: days between the interview and the election day (23 February 2025), used as survey date fixed effects,
- `pol_interest`: political interest as an ordered factor,
- `turnout_int_dummy`: intends to vote (10 on the 1-10 scale or already voted by mail),
- `zs_int`: vote intention with the party names of the long data (CDU and CSU combined),

The table shows the size of the experimental groups.

```{r recodes}
data_federal <- data_federal %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      group,
      levels = c("control", "treatment_small", "treatment"),
      labels = c("Control", "Treatment (5)", "Treatment (500)")
    ),
    # Days before the election (survey date fixed effects), computed in 01_create_replication_data.R
    lead_time = factor(lead_time),
    pol_interest = factor(
      pol_interest,
      levels = c("Überhaupt nicht", "Weniger stark", "Mittelmäßig", "Stark", "Sehr stark")
    ),
    turnout_int = factor(turnout_int, levels = rev(levels(turnout_int))),
    # Turnout intention: 10 on the 1-10 scale or already voted by mail
    turnout_int_dummy = case_when(
      turnout_int %in% c("10", "Ich habe bereits Briefwahl gemacht.") ~ "ja",
      turnout_int %in% as.character(1:9) ~ "nein",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    turnout_int_dummy = factor(turnout_int_dummy, levels = c("nein", "ja")),
    # Vote intention with the party names of the long data
    zs_int = case_when(
      list_vote_int %in% c("CDU", "CSU") ~ "CDU/CSU",
      list_vote_int %in% c("B'90/Die Grünen") ~ "Greens",
      list_vote_int %in% c("Die Linke") ~ "Left",
      list_vote_int %in% c("SSW", "Eine andere Partei") ~ "Others",
      list_vote_int == "ungueltig" ~ "Invalid",
      list_vote_int == "Weiß ich nicht" ~ "Don't know",
      TRUE ~ list_vote_int
    )
  ) %>%
  set_variable_labels(
    lead_time         = "Number of days before the election the interview took place",
    turnout_int_dummy = "Turnout intention dummy (10 or mail = yes)"
  )

data_federal %>% count(treatment)
```

The sample composition table (Table B.3) compares the sample with the electorate.
For this, age, vote intention, gender, education, turnout intention and state are grouped into the categories of the official statistics, with English labels.
Respondents who answered "diverse" are counted as men (Men*), as in the statistics of the Federal Returning Officer.
The tables show the distribution of each recoded variable.

```{r recodes_sample_composition}
data_federal <- data_federal %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 30 ~ "18-29",
      age >= 30 & age < 40 ~ "30-39",
      age >= 40 & age < 50 ~ "40-49",
      age >= 50 & age < 60 ~ "50-59",
      age >= 60 ~ "60+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    list_vote_int_eng = case_when(
      list_vote_int %in% c("Eine andere Partei", "SSW", "ungueltig", "Weiß ich nicht") ~ "Other",
      list_vote_int == "B'90/Die Grünen" ~ "Greens",
      list_vote_int == "Die Linke" ~ "Left",
      TRUE ~ list_vote_int
    ),
    list_vote_int_eng = factor(list_vote_int_eng,
      levels = c("AfD", "BSW", "CDU", "CSU", "FDP", "Greens", "Left", "SPD", "Other")
    ),
    gender_eng = case_when(
      gender == "Weiblich" ~ "Women",
      gender == "Männlich" ~ "Men",
      gender == "Divers" ~ "Diverse",
      TRUE ~ gender
    ),
    # Diverse counted as men (Men*)
    gender_eng2 = case_when(gender_eng == "Diverse" ~ "Men", TRUE ~ gender_eng),
    education_eng = case_when(
      education %in% c(
        "Schule beendet ohne Abschluss",
        "Hauptschulabschluss, Volksschulabschluss, Abschluss der polytechnischen Oberschule 8. oder 9. Klasse"
      ) ~ "Low",
      education %in% c(
        "Realschulabschluss, Mittlere Reife, Fachschulreife oder Abschluss der polytechnischen Oberschule 10. Klasse"
      ) ~ "Medium",
      education == "Bin noch Schüler/in" ~ "Still in School",
      education == "Anderen Schulabschluss, und zwar:" ~ NA,
      education %in% c(
        "Fachhochschulreife (Abschluss einer Fachoberschule etc.)",
        "Abitur bzw. erweiterte Oberschule mit Abschluss 12. Klasse (Hochschulreife)"
      ) ~ "High",
      TRUE ~ education
    ),
    education_eng = factor(education_eng,
      levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Still in School")
    ),
    turnout_int_eng = case_when(
      turnout_int_dummy == "nein" ~ "No",
      turnout_int_dummy == "ja" ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    bula_en = case_when(
      bula == "Baden-Württemberg" ~ "Baden-Württemberg",
      bula == "Bayern" ~ "Bavaria",
      bula == "Berlin" ~ "Berlin",
      bula == "Brandenburg" ~ "Brandenburg",
      bula == "Bremen" ~ "Bremen",
      bula == "Hamburg" ~ "Hamburg",
      bula == "Hessen" ~ "Hesse",
      bula == "Mecklenburg-Vorpommern" ~ "Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania",
      bula == "Niedersachsen" ~ "Lower Saxony",
      bula == "Nordrhein-Westfalen" ~ "North Rhine-Westphalia",
      bula == "Rheinland-Pfalz" ~ "Rhineland-Palatinate",
      bula == "Saarland" ~ "Saarland",
      bula == "Sachsen" ~ "Saxony",
      bula == "Sachsen-Anhalt" ~ "Saxony-Anhalt",
      bula == "Schleswig-Holstein" ~ "Schleswig-Holstein",
      bula == "Thüringen" ~ "Thuringia",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

data_federal %>% count(age_group)
data_federal %>% count(gender_eng2)
data_federal %>% count(education_eng)
data_federal %>% count(turnout_int_eng)
data_federal %>% count(list_vote_int_eng)
```

## Response Times

The survey file contains two kinds of response times (in seconds):

- the time spent on the page of the expectation item (`t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit`), the dependent variable of H1 (logged),
- the times of five filler items (birth year, vote intention, eligibility, turnout intention, political interest), from which 22 computes each respondent's baseline speed.

The output summarizes the response time of the expectation item in seconds.

```{r response_times}
time_vars_federal <- c("t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit", baseline_speed_vars)

data_federal <- data_federal %>%
  # Logged response time (H1)
  mutate(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit_log = log(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit))

data_federal %>%
  summarize(
    n_missing = sum(is.na(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit)),
    min = min(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  print_values(digits = 1) # helper
```

## Vote Share Expectations (Long Data)

Respondents gave their expected vote share for seven parties and *Others* on sliders.
The wide data are reshaped to one row per respondent and party, and the official result of the party is joined.
The forecast error is the expected minus the actual vote share (`list_votes_exp_diff`, in percentage points).
Positive values mean the party was overestimated.
The H3 models use these long data.

```{r long}
list_votes_exp_vars_federal <- c(
  "CDU/CSU" = "list_votes_exp_cdu",
  "AfD"     = "list_votes_exp_afd",
  "Left"    = "list_votes_exp_linke",
  "Greens"  = "list_votes_exp_gruene",
  "SPD"     = "list_votes_exp_spd",
  "FDP"     = "list_votes_exp_fdp",
  "BSW"     = "list_votes_exp_bsw",
  "Others"  = "list_votes_exp_other"
)

data_federal_long <- data_federal %>%
  select(
    ResponseId, id_unique, treatment, lead_time,
    age, gender, education,
    list_vote_int, starts_with("ptv_"), pid,
    all_of(list_votes_exp_vars_federal)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(names(list_votes_exp_vars_federal)),
    names_to = "party",
    values_to = "list_votes_exp"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    results_official_federal %>% rename(list_votes_result = result_official),
    by = "party"
  ) %>%
  mutate(list_votes_exp_diff = list_votes_exp - list_votes_result) %>%
  relocate(party, list_votes_exp, list_votes_result, list_votes_exp_diff, .after = id_unique)

data_federal_long %>%
  filter(ResponseId == first(ResponseId)) %>%
  select(party, list_votes_exp, list_votes_result, list_votes_exp_diff) %>%
  print_values() # helper
```

## Individual Accuracy (MAE, RMSE)

The accuracy of each respondent's expectations, the dependent variable of H2:
the mean absolute error (MAE) and, as a robustness check, the root mean squared error (RMSE) of the forecast errors over the eight categories (seven parties and *Others*).
Lower values mean more accurate expectations.

```{r accuracy}
accuracy_federal <- data_federal_long %>%
  group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  summarize(
    list_votes_exp_mae  = mean(abs(list_votes_exp_diff)),
    list_votes_exp_rmse = sqrt(mean(list_votes_exp_diff^2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data_federal <- data_federal %>%
  left_join(accuracy_federal, by = "ResponseId") %>%
  set_variable_labels(
    list_votes_exp_mae  = "MAE List Vote Expectations",
    list_votes_exp_rmse = "RMSE List Vote Expectations"
  )

data_federal %>%
  summarize(across(c(list_votes_exp_mae, list_votes_exp_rmse), list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) %>%
  print_values() # helper

rm(accuracy_federal)
```


# Save

Only the variables used later are kept.

```{r save}
data_federal <- data_federal %>%
  select(
    # IDs and interview
    ResponseId, id_unique, source, interview_date, duration, lead_time,
    # Experiment
    treatment, pledge_expectations,
    # Demographics
    age, age_group, gender, gender_eng, gender_eng2,
    education, education_eng, bula, bula_en,
    # Political variables
    pol_interest, turnout_int, turnout_int_dummy, turnout_int_eng,
    list_vote_int, list_vote_int_eng, zs_int, starts_with("ptv_"), pid,
    # Vote share expectations and accuracy
    all_of(unname(list_votes_exp_vars_federal)),
    list_votes_exp_mae, list_votes_exp_rmse,
    # Response times
    all_of(time_vars_federal), t_list_votes_exp_Page_Submit_log
  )

save(data_federal, file = "data/processed/data_federal.rdata")
save(data_federal_long, file = "data/processed/data_federal_long.rdata")
```
